truths.truth: A provider response carrying usage writes both the normalized input/output pair and the provider's raw usage object onto the provider/request event; a response with no usage writes neither key, not a zero; and a call that burned its budget on a degraded outcome still records what it burned.

Wiring: cadence-core/bin/review-provider.mjs:1350 sets `meta.usage = adapter.extractUsage(res.json)` in `callStructured` before the three degrading exits (D-03/D-04), and :641-643 spreads `usage`/`usage_raw` onto the event only when present (D-11). Adapters at :1097, :1142, :1204 read `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`, `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount`/`candidatesTokenCount+thoughtsTokenCount`, `usage.prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`, and cadence-core/references/provider-api.md:28-32, :49-54, :81-85 names the same fields field-for-field.

truths.truth: Every review fire emits one routing/resolve for the reviewer role whichever backend serves it, so a trace with five provider-served fires holds five resolves.
truths.evidence: The SHIPPED PROSE states the rule correctly and in both places a reader can enter from. cadence-core/references/review-triggers.md:26-33: 'ONE resolve per FIRE, owed before any backend is chosen ... The unit is the FIRE, never the dispatch: a panel naming two providers writes exactly ONE resolve and two `provider/request` events against it, and a fire served by a cross-model provider ALONE - no claude-subagent dispatched, so no lifecycle bracket anywhere - still owes that one resolve. Step 4's "no lifecycle bracket" is a statement about the BRACKET and never about this line.' cadence-core/references/review-cross-model.md:6-11 repeats it in the header for a reader who jumped straight to the branch, and review-triggers.md:204-206 restates it inside the step-4 cross-model bullet. D-06's three out-of-scope paths were correctly left alone (workflows/decision-review.md:69 and workflows/minimalism-review.md:80,134 still say they resolve no routing cell). NO RUN EVIDENCES THE RULE. This phase's own record is a counter-example: corr 1-ab10452a holds 2 cad-reviewer routing/resolve events against 6 provider review calls (all openai, all ok, all six carrying usage). The rule landed mid-run in 67868b46, so the first five fires ran against the pre-fix reference - the shipped prose is not what produced the 2-vs-6, but no record yet shows a run produced under it.

human_checks.name: A fallen-back cross-model fire still gets its return (AC2)
human_checks.expected: Set a real provider API key, force that provider to drop out (name an unresolvable model id for its tier), fire a `blocking` trigger so the empty-set fallback runs, then `node cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs trace render --phase <N>`: the fire has no entry under `unpaired` and its bracket carries a token figure rather than `unrecorded`.
human_checks.why_human: Out-of-reach resource, not an unexercised probe. It needs a live provider credential and a deliberately induced provider failure against it; nothing in this tree can manufacture a real drop-out on a real key, and no fallback occurred in this phase's run to observe after the fact.

human_checks.name: One routing resolve per review fire (AC5)
human_checks.expected: On the next full run whose review fires are all provider-served, count `routing/resolve` events for the cad-reviewer role against provider review calls in `trace render --phase <N>`: five fires hold five resolves. This is a COUNT and not a join - the resolve event carries no trigger field (D-12).
human_checks.why_human: No probe exercised it, and none can here. The shipped prose states the rule correctly in both places a reader enters from (review-triggers.md:26-33 and review-cross-model.md:6-11), but the criterion is a count over a future run's record, and this phase's own record is a counter-example produced under the pre-fix reference: 2 resolves against 6 provider review calls under corr 1-ab10452a, with the rule landing mid-run in 67868b46. Only a run made entirely after that commit can settle it.

human_checks.name: /cad-report prints a reviewer cost line (AC6)
human_checks.expected: Run `/cad-report <N>` three times and read the PRINTED output: (a) a phase with recorded provider usage prints a `Cross-model reviews` line carrying a cost figure; (b) a phase whose provider events carry no usage key prints `unrecorded` and never `0`; (c) a scope with no provider review call prints no such line at all. Re-read the figures with `trace render --phase <N>` at check time rather than trusting the ones in reports/plan-2.md, which move as the record grows.
human_checks.why_human: The user deferred this to a human checkpoint. Separately, report.md is model-executed prose with no executor, so no automated command exercises the printed line; the projection feeding it is verified (provider_spend answers {calls:129, tokens:50424, unrecorded:123} on this record) but the rendering of it is not.
